name: Indian Railway Catering & Tourism Corporation Ltd
about: Incorporated in 1999, IRCTC is a Navratna (Category 1, Central Public Sector Enterprises ) and the only company authorized by the Indian government to provide online railway tickets, catering services, and packaged drinking water at railway stations and trains in India [1]

sections.one_liner: Railways' monopoly ticketing and catering arm: revenue grows 18%, but mix shift has pushed margins below the 30% target.
business: Navratna CPSE under Ministry of Railways; sole authorised online rail ticketing, catering and station drinking-water provider. [AR FY26]
FY26 segments: Catering ₹2,399cr (46%), Internet Ticketing ₹1,536cr (30%), Tourism ₹890cr (17%), Rail Neer ₹391–407cr (8%). [AR FY26]
Q1FY27 revenue mix: catering 54%, ticketing 26%, tourism 12%, Rail Neer 8%. Ticketing share fell about 4pts from the FY26 level. [Q1FY27 call]
Ticketing is the profit engine: ₹361cr at 80% margin is about ₹289cr EBITDA, roughly 75% of Q1 EBITDA (₹387cr) on 26% of revenue. [Q1FY27 call]
financial_snapshot: Q1FY27: revenue ₹1,370cr (+18.1% YoY), EBITDA ₹387cr, PAT ₹330cr (-0.3% YoY). OPM 28% vs 34% a year ago. [Numbers]
TTM: revenue ₹5,425cr, EBITDA ₹1,655cr (30.5% OPM), PAT ₹1,392cr. Revenue growth is not reaching profit. [Numbers]
ROCE 46.1%, ROE 34.4%, but ROCE has slid from 54% in FY24 as margins compress. [Numbers]
Mcap ₹34,984cr, P/E 25.4x, P/B 8.1x, yield 2.04%. Price ₹437 is the 52-week low, 40% below the ₹730 high. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue 3y CAGR 13.8% (₹3,541cr→₹5,215cr) vs EBITDA CAGR about 9.3% and PAT CAGR 11.5%. Operating leverage is negative. [Numbers]
OPM down every year: 36%→34%→33%→32% (FY23–26), then 27% and 28% in the last two quarters. [Numbers]
Mix drift explains it: catering grew 33.8% at 9.29% margin while ticketing grew 0.5% at 80% margin. [Q1FY27 call]
Quarterly PAT has stalled at ₹326–330cr for two quarters, below the ₹394cr Q3FY26 peak, despite 15–18% revenue growth. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings ₹81cr against net worth ₹4,309cr; D/E 0.02, flat at 0.02–0.03 over four years. Effectively debt-free. [Numbers]
Debtor days rose from 118 to 132 (FY23–26). Management says about 80% is owed by Railways; HST billing fix is not due until end-FY27. [Numbers] [Q2FY26 call]
Working-capital days moved from 3 to 40 (peak 56 in FY25). The CCC swing from -1,221 to +132 days looks like a data break, as FY26 inventory days are missing. [Numbers]
cash_quality: CFO/PAT averaged 0.78 over FY24–26. FY25 was the weakest at 0.63; FY26 recovered to 0.91 (₹1,273cr vs ₹1,393cr). [Numbers]
FCF rose from ₹744cr to ₹1,196cr (FY23–26). Capex is light: just ₹77cr in FY26. FCF yield is about 3.4%. [Numbers]
FY26 dividend of ₹720cr is covered 1.7x by FCF. About ₹650cr of net-worth growth shows the rest is retained, not consumed. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: The call cited Q4FY26 PAT of ₹447cr; the numbers show ₹326cr. The ₹121cr gap is unexplained in the material. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
The '30% normalised EBITDA' aspiration conflicts with 27% and 28% prints. One-offs (₹24cr) add only about 1.8pts to Q1, giving roughly 30%. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
Q3 pitched non-convenience fees (₹150cr, +26%) as the growth lever. By Q1 they had fallen to ₹113cr, which management blamed on removing ads. [Q3FY26 call] [Q1FY27 call]
Rail Neer story contradicts itself: Q3 said 50–60% of demand served; Q1 cited 17.77 lakh capacity vs 15.5 lakh demand. Revenue grew just 2.8%. [Q3FY26 call] [Q1FY27 call]
guidance: Medium-term growth: catering about 15%, tourism about 20%, IT non-convenience about 10%. EBITDA margin 'aspiring' to 30%. [Q4FY26 call]
Margin repair in FY27–28: catering back to 10–12% (from 9.29%), ticketing back to 80–85% (from 80%). [Q1FY27 call]
Tourism to cross ₹1,000cr in FY28 from ₹890cr, implying about 6% growth, well below the 20% guide. Non-convenience fee target ₹150cr vs ₹113cr. [Q1FY27 call]
Rail Neer capex: Ambernath 2→3 lakh and Danapur 1→2 lakh bottles in FY27; four greenfield plants targeted for FY28. [Q1FY27 call]
Convenience fee growth of 5–7% a year continues; no fee revision planned despite fees unchanged since 2019. RBI iPay response expected in FY27. [Q1FY27 call] [Q4FY26 call]

ledger.delivered: Not yet reported; Q2FY27 not in the numbers

bull: 89% share of reserved tickets at 80% margin is about 75% of EBITDA, with zero debt and ROE 34.4%. [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]
Valuation has reset: P/E 25.4x at the 52-week low, 40% off the high, with a 2.04% yield and FCF covering the dividend 1.7x. [Numbers]
Volume pipeline: 20 Vande Bharat sleepers this year, 260 sets planned. Q1 revenue +18.1%, with one-offs of ₹24cr set to ease. [Q1FY27 call] [Q3FY26 call] [Numbers]
bear: High-margin ticketing grew 0.5% with the fee frozen since 2019. Growth is coming from about 9%-margin catering, so PAT is flat at -0.3%. [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]
Margin has compressed from 36% to 28%, and four of the last five guidance items checkable in the ledger were missed. [Numbers]

Pricing power is administered: catering prices are set by the Ministry, and 5% GST without input credit applies on prepaid trains. Debtor days are 132, mostly owed by the parent. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
questions: Q4FY26 PAT: the call said ₹447cr, reported ₹326cr. What explains the gap?
Which quarter returns to 30% EBITDA, and is that excluding or including one-offs?
Has the Railway Board been formally approached on convenience fee revision since 2019?
Rail Neer: is demand coverage 50–60% or full? Reconcile capacity vs demand.

annual_report.business: IRCTC, a Navratna CPSE under Ministry of Railways, operates digital ticketing, hospitality, tourism, and packaged drinking water services for Indian Railways. Revenue from Internet Ticketing (₹1,536 crore), Catering (₹2,399 crore), Tourism (₹890 crore), and Rail Neer (₹407 crore). Serves millions of passengers annually.

segments.name: Catering
segments.comment: 63+ crore meals annually across 1,450+ trains; 12.88% YoY growth

segments.name: Internet Ticketing
segments.comment: 88.74% of reserved bookings; 14.5 lakh daily; 7.66% growth

segments.name: Tourism
segments.comment: Bharat Gaurav trains, luxury journeys, pilgrimage circuits; 19.49% revenue growth

segments.name: Rail Neer
segments.comment: Packaged drinking water; 20 plants; 20.65% profit growth

annual_report.revenue_mix: Product-portfolio: Catering (46%), Internet Ticketing (30%), Tourism (17%), Rail Neer (8%). Operations span 1,450+ trains, 420+ railway stations, all-India network.
strategy: Expand digital capabilities and mobile-first ticketing platform adoption
Grow tourism portfolio including Bharat Gaurav trains and circuits
Build integrated travel ecosystem for end-to-end passenger journeys
Deepen engagement through co-branded partnerships and digital services
Advance environmental stewardship and community development initiatives
annual_report.outlook: India's travel economy expanding with rising domestic tourism. IRCTC positioned to support growth through strengthened digital platforms, expanded tourism offerings, and superior passenger experiences.
annual_report.capex_plans: Infrastructure enhancements: Next Generation e-Ticketing platform (37,000 tickets/minute capacity), AI-enabled monitoring, solar installations. No forward capex guidance.
